amendments.rule: **A cognate infinitive absolute the ASV renders with a distinct adverbial word takes that word as its own unit.** The finite cognate verb retains its subject, auxiliaries and lexical verb phrase under rule 17, while the infinitive absolute takes the English word spent on its emphasis and heads on that word: `פָּקֹד יִפְקֹד` → *will surely visit* gives *surely* to the infinitive absolute and *will visit* to the finite verb, and `הָשֵׁב יָשִׁיב` → *will fully requite* gives *fully* and *will requite* on the same terms. This is rule 2's smallest defensible unit rather than rule 30 fusion, because the ASV has written a separate English word for the infinitive absolute's contribution. The finished corpus has 34 Qal infinitive-absolute units across 26 chapters independently aligned to *surely*, *utterly*, *indeed*, *diligently* or *certainly*, all headed on the intensifier. **Read that word as whatever the ASV has spent on the emphasis, and not as a class of intensifying adverbs.** Where the clause is a rhetorical, concessive or conditional one and the ASV writes a minimizing or restrictive adverb in that same slot, the word is the infinitive absolute's on exactly the same terms and heads its unit: `וְאָבִיהָ יָרֹק יָרַק בְּפָנֶיהָ` → *If her father had* ***but*** *spit in her face* gives *but* to the infinitive absolute and *had spit* to the finite verb. **And read *word* as one English rendering rather than one English token, exactly as rule 30 reads its own one-word condition.** Where the ASV spends a fixed multi-word adverbial expression on that emphasis, the whole expression is the infinitive absolute's one unit: no part of it is `added`, no part of it is a neighbouring morpheme's, and the unit heads under rules 24 and 31 on the content word the expression turns on rather than on one of its function words. `הֲיָכוֹל יָכְלוּ אֱלֹהֵי גּוֹיֵי הָאֲרָצוֹת` → *Were the gods of the nations of the lands* ***in any wise*** *able* gives *in any wise* to the infinitive absolute, headed on *wise*, while the finite verb keeps its bare *able* and the interrogative particle keeps the fronted copula rule 20 gives it; the *in* and the *any* state nothing on their own and no morpheme in the clause answers to either, so rule 15's supplied determiner and rule 11's function-word priority do not reach them. But read what stands in the clause before taking the whole expression: where a negative, a `כֹּל` or another morpheme is itself what a word of that expression says, that morpheme takes it under rules 35, 41 and 48 and the infinitive absolute takes only the rest. Test by subtraction as rules 16, 31 and 43 do: drop the English word and ask whether the infinitive absolute has lost its whole rendering or only the clause has lost a shade of force. Do not mark such a word `added` under rule 30 or fold it into the finite verb, into a conjunction or into a negative standing beside it, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also*: a morpheme stands in the clause for it, no other morpheme answers to it, and the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. Where the ASV writes no distinct adverbial word at all for the infinitive absolute, the ordinary rules decide what, if anything, realizes it.
amendments.why: 2CH.32.13 renders the cognate infinitive absolute of `הֲיָכוֹל יָכְלוּ` by the three-word *in any wise*, which rule 56 as written did not contemplate: its operative sentences say *word* throughout, and a pass reading them strictly would either split the expression, hand *any* to a determiner rule, or mark part of it `added`. The widening is the reading rule 30 already states for its own one-word condition (*because of*, *by reason of*) and rule 40 states for a neighbouring morpheme's compound rendering (*round about*), so it introduces no principle the contract lacks and contradicts nothing in the corpus, whose 34 infinitive-absolute units are all single-word intensifiers and simply do not reach this shape. The closing carve-out keeps it from swallowing a word another present morpheme licenses, which is where an unqualified widening would have done damage.

conventions: Rule 31's class-noun tie guidance was applied by the test the rule states and not by the shape of the English phrase. Where the ASV writes the generic noun alone for a Hebrew word of that same class in this chapter, the head stays on that noun: מִסְכְּנוֹת -> *store houses* heads on *houses*, because בַּיִת -> *house* stands at 2CH.32.21, and תִּירוֹשׁ -> *new wine* heads on *wine*, which is what the word is. Where it does not, the noun is a supplied generic and the head is the modifier: מִגְדָּנוֹת -> *precious things*, חֲסָדָיו -> *good deeds*, גִּבּוֹר -> *mighty men*, רְחוֹב -> *broad place*, בָּמָה -> *high places*, מַעֲרָב -> *west side*, זֹאת -> *this manner*, יְהוּדִית -> *the Jews language*.

Where the ASV subordinates to a written antecedent something the Hebrew writes as a phrase rather than a clause — an appositional nominal or a bare prepositional phrase — the supplied relative answers to no morpheme and is its own `added` unit under rule 55, while the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate morpheme: מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי הָאָדָם -> *which are the work of men's hands* at 2CH.32.19 leaves *which* added and gives *are* to מַעֲשֶׂה under rule 20, and כָּל בִּלְבָבוֹ -> *all that was in his heart* at 2CH.32.31 leaves *that* added and gives *was in* to the בְּ under rule 49. Rule 46's nominal-recasting paragraph was read and set aside in both: it reaches a noun the ASV recasts as head noun and relative clause together, and here the antecedent is a different written word that already holds its own English.

An emphatic הוּא standing before a written proper name takes the whole determiner expression the ASV writes for it and the name keeps only its own word: הוּא יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ -> *the same Hezekiah* at 2CH.32.12 and *This same Hezekiah* at 2CH.32.30. Head on the demonstrative word where the ASV writes one (*This*), and on the identifying word where it writes only an article beside it (*same*); neither word is `added` and the name is not a home for either.

report: Checked all 75 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for the split the table cannot see: supplied English marked `added` in one verse and folded into a licensing morpheme in another. The five `added` units (v.5 *it*, v.19 *which*, v.25 *done*, v.31 *the business of*, v.31 *that*) each have a parallel elsewhere in the chapter that was handled the same way, so nothing there is in surplus on one side only.

One real split, in the head of a single Hebrew noun rendered by a modifier plus a generic English noun. 2CH.32.23 מִגְדָּנוֹת -> *precious things* heads on *precious*, and every other such rendering in the chapter heads on the lexeme-bearing modifier — *mighty men* (v.3, v.21), *broad place* (v.6), *high places* (v.12), *this manner* (v.15), *the Jews language* (v.18), *west side* (v.30) — but 2CH.32.32 חֲסָדָיו -> *good deeds* heads on *deeds*. Rule 31's class-noun tie guidance does not reach that unit: it asks whether the ASV writes the English noun alone for a Hebrew word of the same class in the verse, in the passage, or as its ordinary rendering of the word before it, and no bare *deeds* is written for חֶסֶד — the chapter's own deed-words are דָּבָר -> *acts* and מַעֲשֶׂה -> *work*, *works*. Patched 2CH.32.32 to head on *good*, with the competing head named in the unit note under rule 8.

2CH.32.28's *store houses* and *new wine* stand as accepted, and the patch is not a chapter-wide preference for the modifier. There the tie guidance's own condition is met: the ASV writes a bare *house* for בַּיִת at 2CH.32.21 in this same chapter, and תִּירוֹשׁ is wine, so *store* and *new* are the ASV's specifiers distinguishing one class word from another, exactly as rule 31's *the fierce lion* is.

Verified consistent and left alone: determiner counting (an article unrepresented wherever a demonstrative or possessive carries the phrase's one determiner, v.1, v.14, v.24; the written *the* going to the present article on הָעֶלְיוֹן before a supplied one, v.30); supplied *the* on construct nouns and on the middle term of multi-level chains; dative and benefactive לְ silenced wherever the ASV writes a bare object (v.12, v.15, v.24, v.27, v.29, v.33); all ten object markers unrepresented; the fronted question auxiliary to the particle where one stands (v.11 *Doth*, v.12 *Hath*, v.13 *Were*) and to the verb where none does or where the interrogative already holds a word (v.9 *did send*, v.10 *do trust*), with v.13's first הֲ unrepresented for a question marked by inversion alone; coordinator-plus-subordinator pairs headed on the coordinator (v.2, v.21, v.23, v.26); and the fusions מִפְּנֵי, מִלִּפְנֵי, לִפְנֵי, מִחוּץ, לְמַטָּה, עַל־מָה, אַחֲרֵי־כֵן and וְ+אַל -> *nor*/*neither*, each splitting only where the ASV spends a word on each morpheme (בְּתוֹךְ -> *through the midst*).

BSB: 40 disagreements, all on the documented convention boundary and none a genuine error. Thirteen articles, five object markers and fourteen prepositions are the standing difference (BSB attaches a morpheme to its phrase where the ASV's recasting leaves it no English); the three waws (v.3, v.21, v.28) are clauses the ASV opens bare; v.13's הֲ is a question marked by inversion; v.28's בְהֵמָה is the second half of a distributive repetition the ASV renders once under rule 22; v.31's כֵן is left unrendered beside the waw's *Howbeit*; and v.15's לֹא is absorbed in the אַף כִּי idiom *how much less*, where the ASV writes no *not*. Nothing here should be changed to move the 95.3% figure.

One single-verse judgment a later reader may want to revisit, recorded here rather than patched because it is not a cross-verse split: 2CH.32.22 מִסָּבִיב -> *on every side* divides *on* to מִן and *every side* to סָבִיב. Rule 40's compound-rendering paragraph, and its count of 144 סָבִיב -> *round about* units, would instead keep the whole expression with the adverb and leave the מִן unrepresented, since *on* carries nothing of מִן's ablative sense. The accepted division is defensible under rule 11 and was left as the verse pass made it.
